issue_context.title: Imported value generates reference errors with Webpack 5
issue_context.body:
# Bug report



**What is the current behavior?**

The code below will generate `Uncaught ReferenceError: Subscriber is not defined` error when executed, when built with webpack@5.
```js
import { share } from 'rxjs/operators';
console.log(share);
```

**If the current behavior is a bug, please provide the steps to reproduce.**

Reproduction: https://github.com/csvn/webpack-import-error-issue-reproduction

```js
const { join } = require('path');

module.exports = {
  mode: 'development',
  devtool: 'source-map',
  resolve: {
    mainFields: ['es2015', 'module', 'main']
  },
  devServer: {
    contentBase: [join(__dirname, 'public'), join(__dirname, 'node_modules')]
  }
};
```

1. Clone the repo and run `npm install`
2. Run `npm start` to run `webpack-dev-server`
3. Open http://localhost:8080
4. There will be a error in the console with reference error related to `Subscriber`

> Note: I used a `importmap` and native ESM module to run the same/similar code without Webpack, to see if native ESM modules had problems with with importing `rxjs`. It worked as it should for me (with experimental features JS feature flag in Chrome)

<!-- A great way to do this is to provide your configuration via a GitHub repository -->
<!-- The most helpful is a minimal reproduction with instructions on how to reproduce -->
<!-- Repositories with too many files or large `webpack.config.js` files are not suitable -->
<!-- Please only add small code snippets directly into this issue -->
<!-- https://gist.github.com is a good place for longer code snippets -->
<!-- If your issue is caused by a plugin or loader, please create an issue on the loader/plugin repository instead -->

**What is the expected behavior?**

The code snippet below will run and log the function without generating errors at runtime with webpack@5.
```js
import { share } from 'rxjs/operators';
console.log(share);
```

I've gone through the `rxjs` code, and can't see anything that would produce this error. Webpack do not show any build errors at all. For some reason, it seems Webpack does not correctly transform the `Subscriber` value inside `ConnectableObservable.js`:

```js
// ./node_modules/rxjs/_esm2015/internal/observable/ConnectableObservable.js
class RefCountSubscriber extends Subscriber { ...
// ./node_modules/rxjs/_esm2015/internal/operators/refCount.js
class RefCountSubscriber extends _Subscriber__WEBPACK_IMPORTED_MODULE_0__.Subscriber { ...
```

<!-- "It should work" is not a helpful explanation -->
<!-- Explain exactly how it should behave -->

**Other relevant information:**
webpack version: 5.0.0-beta.14
Node.js version: 13.10.0
Operating System: Windows 10
Additional tools: -
comments: The closest similar issue I could find was https://github.com/webpack/webpack/issues/10542, but it does not seem to be exactly the same.
